_doc: New findings of the correspondence lane (ids F-C<module><nn>, CONVENTIONS.md record shape). For the orchestrator to merge into findings/audit/11.json and 12.json. Existing findings this lane corroborates are listed under 'corroborated' with the new evidence.

findings.title: Relationships the wire schema admits are refused once s+p+o exceed an undocumented key-length limit
findings.intended: specs/213-graph-revision-ledger/contracts/changeset.schema.json:7-8 (NodeId maxLength 256, Name128 maxLength 128 for the tuple's s, o and p); Graph_KG.rdf_edges declares s, o_id VARCHAR(256) and p VARCHAR(128) (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:37-39).
findings.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-capacity): a commit of create_relationship with s = o of 194 characters and p of 97 commits; with s = o of 195 and p of 97 (and with 256/128) it is refused with failed_op 'insert relationship failed: ... <SUBSCRIPT>%SQLInsert+21^Graph.KG.rdfedges.1 ^t52S.BWr6.3(...)': the table's own unique index u_spo_graph_ekey (schema.py:44) cannot hold the key. The refusal is clean (nothing written). The ledger's tuple index ^IVG.Ledger("tuple", s, p, o, graphKey) would overflow one character later (s = o = 195, p = 97 still fits a read; read-only probe), so widening the table index would move the failure into AllocStmt (LedgerApply.cls:165) and genesis Capture (LedgerGenesis.cls:47). A ledger-bypassing create_edge is refused by the same index (SQLCODE -415).
findings.remedy: Document one combined key-length limit for (s, p, o, graph) that every store holding the tuple as subscripts can carry (rdf_edges' unique index, ^KG("out"/"in"), ^IVG.Ledger("tuple")), validate it before the transaction (client and ApplyAll) with its own error, and align the wire schema; or key the indexes by a hash of long values.
findings.notes: Clean failure, no corruption: availability and contract. Reproduce: experiment/playbook-completion/correspondence/tools/capacity.py.

findings.title: The commit does not enforce the wire schema's length limits, and reports violations as a ledger inconsistency
findings.intended: changeset.schema.json: message maxLength 4000 (:189), idempotency_key maxLength 256 (:193), qualifier values maxLength 4000 (:46); errors.py:87-88 LedgerInconsistencyError 'The ledger's own structures disagree with each other'; CommitError codes (changeset.schema.json:288-311).
findings.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-capacity), every refusal clean (no state change): idempotency_key of 257 characters -> inconsistent 'revision row save failed: ERROR #7201 Datatype value ...' (LedgerRevision MAXLEN, Ledger.cls:554-555); of 600 -> inconsistent '<SUBSCRIPT> CommitInTxn+35^Graph.KG.Ledger.1 ^IVG.Ledger("idem",...)' (Ledger.cls:457); message of 4,001 -> inconsistent #7201; a qualifier value of 4,000,000 -> inconsistent '<MAXSTRING> %GetNext+30^%Iterator.Object.1'. Each surfaces in Python as LedgerInconsistencyError. Conversely a qualifier value of 1,000,000 characters (schema maximum 4000) is accepted and recorded.
findings.remedy: Validate the changeset and its metadata against the published limits before TSTART (and in Changeset.validate), refusing with a validation code (failed_op with op_index, or a new code) instead of 'inconsistent'; keep 'inconsistent' for disagreements of the ledger's own structures.
findings.notes: Operators alerting on LedgerInconsistencyError would page on an over-long idempotency key.

findings.title: A detach delete assigns statement ids to unrecorded incident edges in storage order
findings.intended: specs/213 FR-011 (detach cascades in statement-id order); playbook §3.4 storage-order / §3.6 row-permutation: results must not depend on row insertion order.
findings.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-row-permutation): a recorded node pm|1 with three unrecorded (ledger-bypassing) edges to pm|a, pm|b, pm|c inserted in the orders abc, cba, bca; delete_node(pm|1, detach) records the same three delete_rel records each time, but statement ids 1, 2, 3 go to the edges in insertion order (LedgerApply.cls:385-398: incident edges from a SELECT without ORDER BY; AllocStmt in cursor order). Recorded content without the ids is identical.
findings.remedy: Order the incident-edge SELECT by (s, p, o_id, graph_id) before allocating ids, if statement identity is meant to be a function of the logical state.
findings.notes: Working assumption: harmless (replay compares content; ids are internal), recorded because identical logical states give different histories.

findings.title: Every node_not_found refusal is decoded as a create_relationship failure with relationship-only advice
findings.intended: errors.py:91-92 (NodeNotFoundError: 'A relationship operation references a node that does not exist'); the server emits node_not_found also for add_label, remove_label, set_prop, remove_prop and delete_node (LedgerApply.cls:290, 299, 315, 325, 380) besides create_rel (:459-460); FR-008 asks for the failing op's index and reason.
findings.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-trace-ext, op commit-failed-op): a changeset whose add_label names a missing node is refused with failed_op/node_not_found; the client raises NodeNotFoundError 'create_relationship failed: node 'nope|1' does not exist. Add upsert_node('nope|1') to the changeset, or set auto_stub_missing_nodes=True' (errors.py:120-125, from_commit_error :187-193). op_index and reason are kept; the message names the wrong operation and advice (auto_stub_missing_nodes only stubs relationship endpoints, changeset.py:205-209) that cannot fix a node operation.
findings.remedy: Build the message from the op index and the server's reason (or narrow NodeNotFoundError to create_rel/upsert_rel refusals).
findings.notes: The orchestrator's decoder-map-ledger check verifies the code -> exception map, not the message.

findings.title: EraseNodes fails on a prefix longer than the subscript limit instead of erasing nothing
findings.intended: Eraser.cls:307-321 (EraseNodes removes every node whose id starts with the prefix; 0 means nothing matched); the redaction of the same target answers complete with nothing matched.
findings.observed: Live AUDITC (corr-capacity): EraseNodes("", <10,000 characters>) throws 'erase failed on cursor ivgErasePrefix with SQLCODE -400 (<SUBSCRIPT> ... ^t52S.XCFT.4(...))' (Eraser.cls:333-339); nothing changes. LedgerRedact.Redact with a 10,000-character prefix answers ok.
findings.remedy: Return 0 for a prefix longer than any node_id can be (256), or validate the prefix length up front.
findings.notes: No id can match such a prefix (node_id VARCHAR(256)).

corroborated.note: EraseNodes and EraseGraph complete in 6-14 ms while a probe holds ^IVG.Ledger("head") exclusively; their journal shows ^IVG.Ledger stmt/tuple KILLs before the probe releases.

Both trials: conformance step rules and alpha steps pass per transaction, the final state has the committed edge (G,u,R,v) live without a statement entry, which neither serial order of the two committed transactions produces.
Enable waits for the head lock at Ledger.cls:266 inside its transaction, after the state read at :254.
Redact's first head-lock wait is in Batch (LedgerRedact.cls:282), after the unlocked opening reads; no journaled write precedes it.
The post-commit property write is a store change outside any ledger record (premise P-C02 instance).
